A cascade: the counted baseline, a small network over exact features and text channels for every file, then a tuned code decoder reading question and shortlisted file together with relation tokens, a history token and the latest events; the stricter cut-off rule with marked examples. Every veto read: nearest W1 (outside the shortlist the dense channel is two vectors, beside pair-specific channels) and W4 (the event list is short, the bank covers all history). M6 in part: far files are reached by content and by names the decoder proposes; structure stops at two hops, and a right file tied only by a longer route or by a similar past unit of work has no channel. Everything exact is computed for every file alive (kernel bank on two clocks, 468 typed path types, a lag curve counted per repository, reach by any path, echo, text); the score is the baseline plus boosted trees over that record plus, in a shortlist, a tuned joint reader whose head also reads the exact record; stages trained on offsets from fits that did not see the example; one score ranks every file. Every veto read: nearest W10 (trees, on relative amounts only) and W1 (the cosine channel, never alone). Lacks, in words. An event is weighed by size and age only, never by what it was or by the question. Nothing is per question except the offset and the start kind; the error question has no part of its own. M4: the reader's cut-off rule is the data design's only; nothing keeps it before the validation stretch. Typed composition stops at two links. Outside the shortlist text meaning rests on vectors computed apart. M7 open on rows per question, processor hours for the record, pairs per hour, and on whether a reader of a few hundred million parameters is what the compute allows or only an assumption.

A linear first stage over cheap channels for every file, then a two-layer question-rooted propagation over the shortlist in which each candidate's input is the tuned decoder's joint reading of question and file, with per-event gates and ungated exact columns kept beside them; small parts per question; the stricter cut-off rule; shortlists from fits on the other half of the clusters. Every veto read: nearest W1 and W5, neither met. M6 in part, as C2: reach by content and proposed names, structure to two hops, no channel for a longer route or a similar past unit. Other lacks: decay monotone only; a file in the shortlist always above one outside. M7 open and the tightest of the four by its own count: the decoder's frozen pass over all content takes about 7 of 24 card-hours at half a billion parameters and too much above that, so the reader's size is held down by the vectors.
